title: fullcycle.bats claims the cycle runs no cargo, reads one file, and misses an env-prefixed command
body:
## Problem

fullcycle.bats:1296 is titled "the shipped fullcycle contains NO cargo invocation", and it reads only lib/cmd/fullcycle (:1322). The cycle does run cargo -- `cargo metadata`, at lib/helpers:1299, whenever a carrier is present -- and the arm's pattern misses a command written with an environment prefix, which is exactly the form helpers:1299 uses. A false claim in a title is a false green waiting for its reader. 0150's critic pass 5 parked it as R3; fixed forward in the bundle on hv's word, 2026-10-03.

## Measured at 2ce9411 (cc's evidence pass)

A planted `CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo build --release` in lib/cmd/fullcycle leaves the arm green; the same line without the prefix turns it red.

## Fix

The arm says what it holds -- fullcycle runs no build or test through cargo -- accepts `NAME=value ` prefixes, and plants the prefixed form as a second line. A second arm holds that the only cargo command in lib/helpers is `metadata --offline --no-deps`.

## Done when

1. The prefixed plant turns the arm red; red at 2ce9411.
2. A cargo build planted in lib/helpers turns the second arm red.

## Resolution

Fixed at cf01591e. The arm says what it holds: lib/cmd/fullcycle runs no cargo command outside a comment, so the cycle builds and tests only through its build and test commands, which may themselves be cargo, devbin's shipped `cargo test` included. The cargo the cycle runs on its own is lib/helpers' `cargo metadata`, which a second arm now pins.

One matcher, `cargo_cmd_lines`, serves both arms.
- It reads `cargo` in a command position: at the start of a line, or after a separator, `$(`, a backtick or a brace.
- It looks behind any number of `NAME=value` prefixes, the form lib/helpers writes, and behind the words that put a command there: `if`, `then`, `elif`, `else`, `do`, `while`, `until`, `!`, `{`, `time`, `env`, `command`, `exec`, `nohup`, `nice` and `xargs`.
- It reads a quoted or escaped `cargo` too.
- Only lines whose command is printf or echo are dropped, where any line holding either word was dropped before.
- A grep that fails fails the matcher, and the second arm tells each grep's no-match from its failure the same way. The old `|| true` would have read an error as no hits: a first draft of this fix used a pattern BSD grep refuses, and passed vacuously until its own planted control caught it.

Its stated limits:
- It does not see cargo reached through a variable, through a printf piped into a shell, or behind an option to a wrapper word.
- A quoted value with a separator before `cargo` inside it is read as a command, a false red, which fails safe.

Driven:
- A planted `CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo build --release` in lib/cmd/fullcycle leaves the old arm green and turns the new one red.
- So do `if cargo build`, `! cargo build`, `env CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo build` and `out="$(echo x)"; cargo build`, which critic-shell found the first fold of this fix still missed.
- A planted `cd -- "$1" && CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo build --release` in lib/helpers turns the second arm red.
- The first arm's own control plants ten lines and requires exactly the eight commands among them to be found. The other two only mention cargo: a quoted assignment and a printf.
- Both arms are green under BSD and GNU grep.

The full suite on the landing tree: vc's full suite, on main af758c10 (code at 415ce738) with 0163 v3.1 and 0167 git-am'd, cc's 0155, 0160, 0161 and 0162 applied above them, and 0168, 0165, 0170 and 0171 applied above those, in a fresh clone: 2203 of 2203 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261006-0621), 06:21:47Z to 07:07:05Z; 5 skipped, the expected five: two arms that need a runner with no controlling terminal, two require_command arms whose expected outcome is a skip, and a case-folding disk.
